passages.quote: Centrifugal pumps basically consist of a stationary pump casing and an impeller mounted on a rotating shaft.
The pump casing provides a pressure boundary for the pump and contains channels to properly direct the suction and discharge flow.

The vanes of the rotating impeller impart a radial and rotary motion to the liquid, forcing it to the outer periphery of the pump casing where it is collected in the outer part of the pump casing called the volute.
This converts the velocity head to static pressure.
A diffuser is a set of stationary vanes that surround the impeller.
In a radial flow pump, the liquid enters at the center of the impeller and is directed out along the impeller blades in a direction at right angles to the pump shaft.
In an axial flow pump, the impeller pushes the liquid in a direction parallel to the pump shaft.
A pump stage is defined as that portion of a centrifugal pump consisting of one impeller and its associated components.

Wearing rings are replaceable rings that are attached to the impeller and/or the pump casing to allow a small running clearance between the impeller and the pump casing without causing wear of the actual impeller or pump casing material.
The stuffing box is a cylindrical space in the pump casing surrounding the shaft.
Packing is material in the form of rings or strands that is placed in the stuffing box to form a seal to control the rate of leakage along the shaft.
Stuffing boxes are normally designed to allow a small amount of controlled leakage along the shaft to provide lubrication and cooling to the packing.

A lantern ring is a perforated hollow ring located near the center of the packing box that receives relatively cool, clean liquid from either the discharge of the pump or from an external source and distributes the liquid uniformly around the shaft to provide lubrication and cooling.
Mechanical seals consist of two basic parts, a rotating element attached to the pump shaft and a stationary element attached to the pump casing.
If flow through the pump is stopped while the pump is still operating, the pump will no longer be adequately cooled and the pump can quickly become damaged.

If the pressure drop is large enough, or if the temperature is high enough, the pressure drop may be sufficient to cause the liquid to flash to vapor when the local pressure falls below the saturation pressure for the fluid being pumped.
This process of the formation and subsequent collapse of vapor bubbles in a pump is called
A cavitating pump can sound like a can of marbles being shaken.
Other indications that can be observed from a remote operating station are fluctuating discharge pressure, flow rate, and pump motor current.
This physical shock creates small pits on the leading edge of the impeller vane.
Cavitation can also cause excessive pump vibration, which could damage pump bearings, wearing rings, and seals.
The net positive suction head available (NPSHA) is the difference between the pressure at the suction of the pump and the saturation pressure for the liquid being pumped.
The net positive suction head required (NPSHR) is the minimum net positive suction head necessary to avoid cavitation.
The condition that must exist to avoid cavitation is that the net positive suction head available must be greater than or equal to the net positive suction head required.
Decreasing the temperature of the liquid decreases the saturation pressure, causing NPSHA to increase.
Therefore, reducing the flow rate through a pump by throttling a discharge valve decreases NPSHR.
The lower the pump head, the higher the flow rate.
Shutoff head is the maximum head that can be developed by a centrifugal pump operating at a set speed.
Pump runout is the maximum flow that can be developed by a centrifugal pump without damaging the pump.
A centrifugal pump is dead-headed when it is operated with no flow through it, for example, with a closed discharge valve or against a seated check valve.
One method for protecting the pump from running dead-headed is to provide a recirculation line from the pump discharge line upstream of the discharge valve, back to the pump's supply source.

One method for ensuring that there is always adequate flow resistance at the pump discharge to prevent excessive flow through the pump is to place an orifice or a throttle valve immediately downstream of the pump discharge.
Runout can lead to cavitation and can also cause overheating of the pump's motor due to excessive currents.
Gas binding of a centrifugal pump is a condition where the pump casing is filled with gases or vapors to the point where the impeller is no longer able to contact enough fluid to function correctly.
Most centrifugal pumps are not self-priming.
A centrifugal pump is started with the discharge valve throttled or closed to minimize the load on the impeller, allowing it to come up to speed quicker.

passages.quote: A positive displacement pump is one in which a definite volume of liquid is delivered for each cycle of pump operation.
The three groups are reciprocating pumps, rotary pumps, and diaphragm pumps.

The volume of liquid moved by the pump in one cycle (one suction stroke and one discharge stroke) is equal to the change in the liquid volume of the cylinder as the piston moves from its farthest left position to its farthest right position.
In general, the effective flow rate of reciprocating pumps decreases as the viscosity of the fluid being pumped increases because the speed of the pump must be reduced.
Rotary pumps operate on the principle that a rotating vane, screw, or gear traps the liquid in the suction side of the pump casing and forces it to the discharge side of the casing.
Slippage is leakage of fluid from the discharge of the pump back to its suction.
The simple gear pump shown in Figure 14 consists of two spur gears meshing together and revolving in opposite directions within a casing.
It is considered as a simple gear pump having only two or three teeth per rotor; otherwise, its operation or the explanation of the function of its parts is no different.
The screw pump is used for pumping viscous fluids, usually lubricating, hydraulic, or fuel oil.
The rotor carries vanes that move in and out as it rotates to maintain sealed spaces between the rotor and the cylinder wall.
The pump construction eliminates any contact between the liquid being pumped and the source of energy.
Therefore, the only factor that effects flow rate in an ideal positive displacement pump is the speed at which it operates.
The characteristic curve for a positive displacement pump operating at a certain speed is a vertical line on a graph of head versus flow.
Positive displacement pumps are normally fitted with relief valves on the upstream side of their discharge valves to protect the pump and its discharge piping from overpressurization.
Annular Linear Induction Pumps are a type of electromagnetic pump used to move liquids without the need for any physical parts like impellers or rotating shafts.

body.alt: Simplified centrifugal pump showing the suction, eye of the impeller, vanes, volute, and discharge.

body.text: The pump casing guides liquid from the suction connection to the center, or eye, of the impeller.
The volute expands in cross-sectional area as it wraps around the casing. It collects high velocity liquid from the impeller and gradually reduces fluid velocity by increasing the flow area.
A diffuser increases efficiency by allowing a more gradual expansion and a less turbulent area for the liquid to reduce in velocity. The growing flow area converts kinetic energy into flow pressure.

body.alt: Impeller surrounded by a ring of stationary diffuser vanes inside the pump casing.

checks.q: What is the purpose of the impeller?
o: To impart a radial and rotary motion to the liquid
To seal the shaft against leakage
To convert pressure to velocity at the discharge
To protect the casing from wear
checks.x: The vanes of the rotating impeller impart a radial and rotary motion to the liquid.

checks.q: What is the purpose of a diffuser in a centrifugal pump?
o: To balance axial thrust
To increase efficiency with a more gradual, less turbulent expansion
To cool the packing
To direct liquid into the eye of the impeller
checks.x: The purpose of the diffuser is to increase the efficiency of the centrifugal pump by allowing a more gradual expansion and less turbulent area for the liquid to reduce in velocity.

body.text: A single-suction impeller lets liquid enter from one direction, and a double-suction impeller from both sides. Impellers can be open, semi-open, or enclosed.
Pumps are also classified by flow: radial, axial, and mixed.

body.alt: Radial flow impeller with liquid leaving at right angles to the shaft.
Axial flow propeller-type impeller with liquid moving parallel to the shaft.

body.text: Mixed flow pumps borrow from both: the blades push liquid out from the shaft at an angle greater than 90°.

body.alt: Mixed flow impeller with liquid leaving at an angle to the shaft.

body.text: A single impeller making more than 150 psid is difficult and costly to design, so multiple impellers go on a common shaft in one casing, each discharging to the suction of the next.

body.alt: Four-stage pump with impellers in series on one shaft.

checks.q: In which pump does the impeller push liquid parallel to the shaft?
o: Axial flow
Radial flow
Mixed flow
Double volute
checks.x: In an axial flow pump, the impeller pushes the liquid in a direction parallel to the pump shaft.

checks.q: What is a pump stage?
o: One rotation of the shaft
One wearing ring and its gland
One impeller and its associated components
One complete pump casing
checks.x: A pump stage is defined as that portion of a centrifugal pump consisting of one impeller and its associated components.

body.alt: Pump cross section labeling the casing, shaft, impeller, volute, stuffing box, gland, packing, lantern ring, and impeller and casing wearing rings.

body.text: A small clearance lets the impeller rotate freely in the casing. Liquid leaking through it from discharge to suction lowers efficiency, and erosion slowly widens it.
They are replaced periodically, which prevents the more costly replacement of the impeller or the casing.
Packing rings are held by a gland. Tightening the adjusting nuts compresses the packing, which expands radially to form a tight seal.
A standard stuffing box will not work if the suction is under a vacuum or the fluid is too hot to cool the packing.
The polished faces of the rotating and stationary elements contact each other to form a seal that prevents leakage along the shaft.

checks.q: What is the purpose of wearing rings?
o: To seal the shaft where it leaves the casing
To distribute cool liquid around the shaft
To convert velocity to pressure
To allow a small running clearance without wearing the impeller or casing
checks.x: Wearing rings are replaceable rings that allow a small running clearance without causing wear of the actual impeller or pump casing material.

checks.q: What is the purpose of packing?
o: To form a seal that controls the rate of leakage along the shaft
To support the impeller
To increase discharge pressure
To keep the pump primed
checks.x: Packing is placed in the stuffing box to form a seal to control the rate of leakage along the shaft.

checks.q: Why is a small amount of leakage allowed along a packed shaft?
o: To provide lubrication and cooling to the packing
To vent gases from the casing
To keep the suction pressure low
To balance the impeller
checks.x: Stuffing boxes are normally designed to allow a small amount of controlled leakage along the shaft to provide lubrication and cooling to the packing.

checks.q: What does a lantern ring do?
o: Distributes relatively cool, clean liquid around the shaft for lubrication and cooling
Holds the packing gland in place
Keeps the impeller centered in the casing
Collects liquid from the impeller
checks.x: A lantern ring receives relatively cool, clean liquid and distributes the liquid uniformly around the shaft to provide lubrication and cooling.

concepts.title: Cavitation and net positive suction head

body.text: The flow area at the eye of the impeller is usually smaller than the suction piping, so entering liquid speeds up and its pressure drops. The greater the flow, the greater the drop.
Vapor bubbles are swept along the vanes. Where local pressure rises above saturation pressure, they abruptly collapse.
That word is cavitation.
NPSHA = Psuction - Psaturation
NPSHA ≥ NPSHR
When a pump takes suction from a tank, the suction pressure is the absolute pressure at the liquid surface, plus the pressure from elevation, less the friction head losses in the suction line.
NPSHA = Pa + Pst - hf - Psat

checks.q: What relationship must exist to avoid cavitation?
o: NPSH required greater than NPSH available
NPSH available equal to zero
Suction pressure below saturation pressure
NPSH available greater than or equal to NPSH required
checks.x: The net positive suction head available must be greater than or equal to the net positive suction head required.

checks.q: A pump takes suction from a tank. Pa = 30 ft, Pst = 12 ft, hf = 4 ft, and Psat = 2 ft. What is NPSHA?
o: 32 ft
36 ft
40 ft
48 ft
checks.x: NPSHA = Pa + Pst - hf - Psat = 30 + 12 - 4 - 2 = 36 ft.

items: Damage to pump impeller, bearings, wearing rings, and seals

body.text: Vapor bubbles collapse against the oncoming vane and cause a physical shock.
Each pit is microscopic, but millions formed over hours or days can literally destroy an impeller.

items: Increase the pressure at the suction of the pump
Reduce the temperature of the liquid being pumped
Reduce head losses in the pump suction piping
Reduce the flow rate through the pump
Reduce the speed of the pump impeller

body.text: Head losses fall with a larger pipe diameter, fewer elbows, valves, and fittings, and a shorter pipe. A slower impeller also lowers NPSHR.

checks.q: Which set lists the three indications of a cavitating pump?
o: Rising suction pressure, no noise, high flow
Noise, fluctuating discharge pressure and flow, fluctuating motor current
Silence, steady flow, low motor current
High oil level, cold bearings, steady flow
checks.x: The indications are noise, fluctuating discharge pressure and flow, and fluctuating pump motor current.

checks.q: Why does throttling a pump's discharge valve help stop cavitation?
o: It lowers the suction pressure
Lower flow rate decreases NPSHR
Higher flow rate raises NPSHA
It raises the saturation pressure
checks.x: Reducing the flow rate through a pump by throttling a discharge valve decreases NPSHR.

checks.q: What physical damage does cavitation do to an impeller?
o: Softening of the packing
Small pits on the leading edge of the vanes
Cracks in the volute
Bending of the shaft
checks.x: The physical shock from collapsing bubbles creates small pits on the leading edge of the impeller vane.

body.text: The impeller spins in the gas bubble but cannot force liquid through the pump, which can lead to cooling problems for the packing and bearings.
Pumps in systems with dissolved gases that are not self-venting should be periodically vented manually.
The casing must be filled with liquid before the pump is started. Most centrifugal pumps are located below the level of their suction source to stay primed.

checks.q: Why are most centrifugal pumps located below the level of their suction source?
o: To shorten the shaft
To remain primed and avoid becoming gas-bound
To lower the discharge pressure
To reduce motor current
checks.x: To ensure that a centrifugal pump remains primed and does not become gas-bound, most centrifugal pumps are located below the level of the source.

concepts.title: Characteristic curve, shutoff head, and runout

body.text: At constant speed, flow through a centrifugal pump depends on the head it develops.

body.alt: Pump head against flow: head is highest at zero flow, at shutoff head, and falls in a downward curve to the runout flow.

body.text: With no flow path, the impeller churns the same liquid. Friction heats it until it flashes to vapor, which can interrupt cooling flow to the packing and bearings.
An automatic flow control device can also give this protection.
Properly designed piping systems are very important for runout protection.

checks.q: What is the shape of a centrifugal pump characteristic curve?
o: A horizontal line at one head
Head is highest at zero flow and falls as flow increases
Head rises steadily as flow increases
A vertical line at one flow rate
checks.x: The lower the pump head, the higher the flow rate, and shutoff head is the maximum head.

checks.q: What is pump runout?
o: The maximum flow a centrifugal pump can develop without damage
The maximum head at a set speed
Operation with no flow through the pump
Loss of prime during operation
checks.x: Pump runout is the maximum flow that can be developed by a centrifugal pump without damaging the pump.

checks.q: How is a centrifugal pump protected from dead-heading?
o: A relief valve on the suction line
An orifice in the suction piping
A larger motor
A recirculation line from the discharge back to the supply source
checks.x: One method is to provide a recirculation line from the pump discharge line upstream of the discharge valve, back to the pump's supply source.

checks.q: How is a centrifugal pump protected from runout?
o: A check valve in the suction line
A vent on the casing
An orifice or throttle valve immediately downstream of the discharge
A recirculation line to the supply tank
checks.x: An orifice or a throttle valve immediately downstream of the pump discharge ensures adequate flow resistance.

checks.q: How does the flow of a positive displacement pump differ from a centrifugal pump?
o: It delivers no flow above shutoff head
It delivers a definite volume each cycle regardless of head
Its flow depends on the head it works against
It gives continuous flow with no separate volumes at any speed
checks.x: The positive displacement pump delivers a definite volume of fluid for each cycle regardless of the head. Flow from a centrifugal pump depends on the head.

checks.q: A pump has two meshing spur gears revolving in opposite directions in a casing. What type is it?
o: Screw-type rotary
Moving vane
Gear-type rotary
Lobe-type rotary

checks.q: A rotor carries vanes that move in and out to keep sealed spaces against the cylinder wall. What type of pump is it?
o: Moving vane
Diaphragm
Lobe-type rotary
Reciprocating piston
checks.x: The rotor carries vanes that move in and out as it rotates to maintain sealed spaces between the rotor and the cylinder wall.

checks.q: What is the main benefit of a diaphragm pump?
o: No check valves are needed
The highest flow of any pump
No contact between the pumped liquid and the source of energy
Unlimited head and capacity
checks.x: The pump construction eliminates any contact between the liquid being pumped and the source of energy.

body.text: As discharge pressure rises, some liquid leaks from the discharge back to the suction, which reduces the effective flow rate.
The relief valve prevents system and pump damage if the discharge valve is shut during operation or if anything else blocks system flow.

checks.q: What is slippage in a positive displacement pump?
o: The rate at which liquid leaks from discharge back to suction
Loss of drive belt tension

examples.title: Checking for cavitation margin
examples.problem: A pump takes suction from an enclosed tank. Pa = 40 ft, Pst = 15 ft, hf = 5 ft, and Psat = 6 ft. The manufacturer gives NPSHR as 20 ft. Will the pump avoid cavitation?
steps: Compare: 44 ft is greater than 20 ft, so NPSHA ≥ NPSHR is met.
examples.answer: Yes. NPSHA is 44 ft, which exceeds the 20 ft required.

facts.q: What is the purpose of wearing rings in a centrifugal pump?
facts.a: They are replaceable rings that allow a small running clearance without wearing the actual impeller or casing.

facts.q: What is the required relationship between NPSHA and NPSHR?
facts.a: NPSHA must be greater than or equal to NPSHR to avoid cavitation.

facts.q: What five changes can reduce cavitation?
facts.a: Raise suction pressure, lower liquid temperature, reduce suction head losses, reduce flow rate, and reduce impeller speed.
The maximum flow a centrifugal pump can develop without damaging the pump.

facts.q: How is a centrifugal pump protected from dead-heading and from runout?
facts.a: Dead-heading: a recirculation line back to the supply source. Runout: an orifice or throttle valve just downstream of the discharge, and proper piping design.

facts.q: What are the three basic groups of positive displacement pumps?
What is the characteristic curve of an ideal positive displacement pump?
facts.a: A vertical line on a graph of head versus flow.

summary.text: A centrifugal pump uses a rotating impeller and a volute or diffuser to convert velocity to pressure.
Keep NPSHA at or above NPSHR to avoid cavitation, which shows as noise and fluctuating pressure, flow, and motor current.
Protect against dead-heading with recirculation and against runout with an orifice or throttle valve.
A positive displacement pump moves a definite volume each cycle and needs a relief valve upstream of its discharge valve.
An ALIP moves liquid metal with a magnetic field and has no impeller or rotating shaft.
summary.cite: Word: ALIP Pumps.docx, slide 1.1 ALIP Intro
